clue.text: The sort of reproduction expected of happy couples?

definitions.text: The sort of reproduction expected of happy couples?

parts.words: The sort of reproduction expected of happy couples?
parts.note: reproduction suggests babies, but here it is the faithful reproduction of recorded sound, while happy couples are expected to be faithful to each other

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of offspring contented couples are supposed to produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduction' tempts you towards childbirth; it is sound reproduction, and the term for accurate audio equipment also names marital faithfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names faithful audio reproduction (hi-fi) and, read literally, great loyalty, which is what spouses expect.

clue.text: Important letter read out in meal

parts.note: high means important, as in high office

indicators.note: a letter read out is spoken, so its spoken name is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: the letter T, whose spoken name is a drink's

explanation.surface: An important letter is read aloud during a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read out' turns the letter T into its sound, a word for a drink; in Britain the answer is an early-evening meal with tea.
explanation.definitionFit: An early-evening British meal with cooked food, bread and cakes, taken with tea.

clue.text: The way the deal is going, you'll get right into profit

definitions.text: The way the deal is going

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, so the letter sits inside the word for profit

parts.note: a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: A trader explains that a deal going well puts you into profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' is not a transaction but pine or fir timber; the direction its fibres run is the wood's pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is softwood timber, and the direction in which its fibres run is the wood's texture pattern.

clue.text: Special fuel cores emit radiation

indicators.note: special suggests a specially prepared version, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Special nuclear fuel cores give off radiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' tells you to rearrange FUEL CORES; the nuclear picture fits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To glow by giving out light after absorbing other radiation, as some minerals do under ultraviolet.

clue.text: Responsibility for tax

definitions.meaning: an obligation or task one is bound to do
a levy on goods, as in customs and excise

explanation.surface: Someone is made accountable for paying a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: An obligation one must fulfil, and also a charge levied on imports.

clue.text: It's helpful lest road gets complicated

indicators.note: when something gets complicated it is tangled and mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guide that helps in case the route becomes confusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets complicated' tells you to rearrange LEST ROAD; the result is a star sailors steered by.
explanation.definitionFit: A guiding star such as the Pole Star, used for navigation, and so anything that helps by guiding.

clue.text: Body making a sort of cross, roughly

parts.note: a T-shaped cross, the tau cross, is one kind of cross
'or so' means roughly, approximately

explanation.surface: Someone's body forming an approximate cross shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' looks like a manner adverb but means 'or so', which follows the T; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human figure, without head or limbs, as in a sculpture.

clue.text: Lady Emma almost had a poet

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
John Milton, the English poet of Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: A gossip item: Lady Emma very nearly took a poet as a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost had' trims HAD to HA. Emma Hamilton was the mistress of Admiral Nelson.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma, Lady Hamilton, wife of the diplomat Sir William and mistress of Nelson.

clue.text: What to drink when it's noon in cool surroundings?

indicators.note: one piece in another means the letter goes inside the word for cool

parts.note: shady means cool, out of the sun

explanation.surface: A question about the right drink to have at midday somewhere pleasantly cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surroundings' fills out the container picture: N is placed in SHADY. In Britain the answer is beer mixed with lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, refreshing pub mixture of beer and lemonade or ginger beer.

clue.text: To some degree, proceeded like a ruler

definitions.meaning: moved on to a university degree, i.e. completed a course and was awarded it
marked off in regular steps, as a measuring rule is marked with scale divisions

explanation.surface: Someone advanced a little, behaving like a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruler' suggests a king or queen, but it is the measuring stick with its scale marks; 'to some degree' is not 'slightly' but 'to a degree' from a university.
explanation.definitionFit: A student who finished a course and took a degree has moved on to it; a rule bearing measuring marks is calibrated with scale divisions.

clue.text: Cutting off the head, open fish

indicators.note: removing the head means the first letter of the word for open is dropped

parts.note: to broach a cask or subject is to open it

explanation.surface: Instructions for preparing a fish: behead it, then open it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting off the head' reads like gutting a fish, but it removes the B from BROACH.
explanation.definitionFit: The roach is a common freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Such a right to work may be academic

definitions.text: Such a right to work may be academic

parts.words: Such a right to work may be academic
parts.note: academic sounds like 'pointless', but it means held by a university lecturer: a permanent post that cannot easily be taken away

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain entitlement to employment may be merely theoretical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Academic' looks like 'of no practical importance'; it really means 'belonging to academics', who may hold a guaranteed permanent position.
explanation.definitionFit: University staff granted security of position hold their post permanently, a right to keep working there.

clue.text: East European schoolboy's written about origin of socialism

indicators.note: something written about another word goes round it, so the schoolboy's name encloses the letter

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil of Eton College, the English public school; the 's is 'is'

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about an Eastern European pupil's essay on the beginnings of socialism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written about' means placed around: S (the first letter of 'socialism') goes inside ETONIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Estonia, a Baltic state, is a person from Eastern Europe.

clue.text: Strindberg's so impressive

definitions.meaning: the first name of the Swedish playwright Strindberg

explanation.surface: Praise for the Swedish dramatist Strindberg as being very impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a comment on Strindberg's work; in fact his forename is one definition and 'impressive' the other, with 'so' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The playwright was August Strindberg; the adjective for majestic or venerable is a homograph of that forename.

clue.text: Climbed aboard, getting pulled inside to have fun

indicators.note: inside means the word for pulled is placed within the phrase for climbed aboard

parts.note: got on means climbed aboard a bus or train
to tow is to pull along

explanation.surface: Someone boards a vehicle and is hauled along for a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: TOW goes inside GOT ON, between its O and N.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for doing something without restraint, enjoying oneself lavishly.

clue.text: Water distribution system needs river as vital support

parts.note: the water mains are the network of pipes supplying a town
the Tay is the longest river in Scotland

explanation.surface: A water supply network that needs a river to keep it going.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief prop or pillar on which something depends; originally the stay supporting a ship's mainmast.

clue.text: Powerful address from man protected by guiding spirit

indicators.note: something protected by another is surrounded by it, so the man's name goes inside

parts.note: a numen is a presiding divinity or guiding spirit
Bert is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man under the care of his guardian spirit delivers a forceful speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a speech but is a street address, 10 Downing Street, home of the British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Downing Street house of the British prime minister is a residence, i.e. address, of power.

clue.text: Feel without confidence, say, leading a mob

indicators.note: leading means coming in front, so this abbreviation goes before the mob

parts.note: sc., short for Latin scilicet, means 'namely' or 'that is to say'
a rabble is a disorderly mob

explanation.surface: Someone unsure of themselves who nonetheless heads a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the abbreviation SC (scilicet, 'that is to say'), placed before RABBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To grope about is to feel around blindly and uncertainly for something.

clue.text: Only one player's required for this operetta

definitions.text: Only one player's required for this
definitions.meaning: a card game played alone, also called solitaire
a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera of 1881, satirising aesthetes

explanation.surface: An operetta that needs only one performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a one-man show; split it after 'this' and the first half is a card game for one, the second a light opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-person card game shares its name with the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.

clue.text: Flower turned into scented dressing

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Po in Italy
made, as in 'made into', means turned into

explanation.surface: A flower converted into perfumed hair cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a river, something that flows; the Po is Italy's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfumed ointment for dressing the hair, as in hair cream.

clue.text: Restoration of outskirts of Amsterdam?

parts.note: the city's name begins with these two letters, which stand in for it here
outskirts are the edges or ends of a place

explanation.surface: A question about rebuilding the suburbs of Amsterdam.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the liberty: 'outskirts of Amsterdam' is read as AM followed by ENDS. Restoration here is the act of making good a wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensation or reparation for a wrong, as in 'make good', a putting right of what was damaged.

clue.text: Like the case of Jekyll and Hyde in novel

definitions.text: Like the case of Jekyll and Hyde
definitions.meaning: Stevenson's story is titled the 'Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde' with this adjective in front
novel as an adjective means new and unusual

explanation.surface: A description of how the Jekyll and Hyde affair is presented in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' is not the book but an adjective meaning odd; 'in' links the two definitions. The scan prints the count as (8), but the grid entry is seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's title calls the case odd, and a novel thing is unfamiliar, odd.

clue.text: Mother's stuff one replaced with new

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out and the other put in its place within the word for stuff

parts.note: stuff means material, fabric
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A mother's fabric, with an old piece swapped for a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother's stuff' looks like one phrase, but 'Mother's' alone is the definition, meaning 'of a mother'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes what belongs to or comes from a parent who bore the child.

clue.text: Discharge from hire, extremely overcome by drink

indicators.note: overcome by means engulfed, so the letters are placed inside the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, first and last, are taken

explanation.surface: A complaint about being let go from a job after being overcome by drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' suggests firing, but it is a watery discharge from eyes or nose; 'extremely' picks the outer letters of 'hire', and 'overcome by' puts them in the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A watery mucous fluid running from the eyes or nose, as with a cold.

clue.text: Recant after torture and get heavenly drink

indicators.note: letters put through torture are twisted out of shape, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A heretic recants under torture and is rewarded with a celestial drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is an Inquisition scene; 'after torture' tells you to rearrange RECANT.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the gods drank this beverage, which conferred immortality.

clue.text: Captured army range in sight

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
ken is the range of sight or knowledge, as in 'beyond our ken'

explanation.surface: An army seized a stretch of land within view.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken prisoner means seized or captured.

clue.text: Tiny amount left in? That's a shock

indicators.note: in means the letter for left goes inside the word for a tiny amount

parts.note: a jot is a very small amount

explanation.surface: Being left with a tiny amount comes as a nasty surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden jerk or bump, or a startling surprise.

clue.text: Use dip-stick to check position of liquid?

definitions.text: Use dip-stick to check position of liquid?

parts.words: Use dip-stick to check position of liquid?
parts.note: a dip-stick sounds like the motorist's oil gauge, but here it is a forked hazel twig that dips to show where underground water lies

explanation.surface: A motorist checks the oil level with a dipstick.
explanation.walkthrough: The car dipstick is the false picture: the stick is a divining rod, and finding the liquid's position is water divining.
explanation.definitionFit: To search for hidden water or minerals with a divining rod, which is said to dip over the spot.

clue.text: Gift that eventually benefits an author

definitions.text: Gift that eventually benefits an author

parts.words: Gift that eventually benefits an author
parts.note: a present voucher redeemable at a bookshop; when it is spent, a writer earns royalties

explanation.surface: A present whose ultimate beneficiary is a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The recipient chooses a book with this voucher, so the writer gains in the end through royalties.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher given as a present and exchanged for books, so some of its value reaches writers.

clue.text: In nice temper, dissipating rudeness

indicators.note: dissipating means scattering or dispersing, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A good mood breaking up into bad manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissipating' tells you to rearrange the twelve letters of IN NICE TEMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolence or cheek, lack of respect for others, is a form of discourtesy.
